content:
Two integrals can look almost the same. One needs by parts, and the other folds in one line by substitution. That small gap decides marks in this chapter. So take this free JEE Indefinite Integrals online test below. It gives 15 MCQs with instant scoring. Also, every answer shows a short worked step. Aim for 12 out of 15.

What JEE asks from integration

  • Standard forms, so you spot them on sight.
  • Substitution, and a function paired with its own derivative.
  • Integration by parts, and the ILATE order for u.
  • Partial fractions, so you split a proper rational function.
  • Trig and algebra tricks, because some integrands need a rewrite.

Formulas to revise first

  • First, the power rule lifts the exponent by one, then divides by it.
  • The integral of 1/x is log of mod x, and never plain log x.
  • For substitution, let u be the inner part, then convert every x.
  • By parts gives u times v, and minus the integral of v du.
  • Add plus C every time, because many answers share one derivative.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Dropping the plus C, and then losing an easy mark.
  • Writing log x, but the safe form stays log of mod x.
  • Leaving a stray x after a substitution, so the integral stalls.
  • Picking the wrong u, because ILATE went ignored.

quiz.title: JEE Indefinite Integration Online Test
quiz.intro: Fifteen JEE-level indefinite integrals across standard forms, substitution, by parts and partial fractions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: Finding a function whose derivative is known is called:
questions.explanation: Integration reverses differentiation. If the derivative of F(x) is f(x), then the integral of f(x) is F(x) + C.

questions.q: In the expression ∫ f(x) dx, the function f(x) is called the:
questions.explanation: The function to be integrated, f(x), is the integrand.
By the power rule, ∫ xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1) + C. So ∫ x³ dx = x⁴/4 + C, and the constant matters.
The derivative of tan x is sec² x, so its antiderivative is tan x + C.
This is a standard form. The derivative of sin⁻¹ x is 1/√(1 − x²).
Substitute u = x², so du = 2x dx. The integral becomes ∫ eᵘ du = e^(x²) + C.
Let u = log x, so du = (1/x) dx. Then ∫ u du = u²/2 + C = (log x)²/2 + C.
Write tan x = sin x/cos x and put u = cos x. The result is −log|cos x| + C = log|sec x| + C.
Take 25 out of the root: (1/5) ∫ dx/√((3/5)² − x²) = (1/5) sin⁻¹(5x/3) + C.
By linear substitution, ∫ (ax + b)ⁿ dx = (ax + b)ⁿ⁺¹/(a(n + 1)) + C.
Partial fractions give A = −1 and B = 2. So the integral is −log|x + 1| + 2 log|x + 2| + C.
Complete the square: 3 + 2x − x² = 4 − (x − 1)². The formula gives (1/4) log|(x + 1)/(3 − x)| + C.

questions.q: ∫ eˣ(1 + x log x)/x dx equals:
questions.explanation: Rewrite as ∫ eˣ(1/x + log x) dx. This fits ∫ eˣ(f + f′) dx = eˣ f with f = log x, so the answer is eˣ log x + C.

questions.q: Why do we add an arbitrary constant C after an indefinite integration?
options: Because the derivative of any constant is zero
questions.explanation: The derivative of a constant is zero, so functions differing by a constant share the same derivative. C stands for that whole family.

faq.q: What is the fastest way to pick a method?
faq.a: Classify the integrand first. A known standard form is instant, a function with its own derivative means substitution, a product of two families means by parts, and a factorable rational function means partial fractions.
ILATE orders function types and tells you which factor to call u in integration by parts. Pick whichever comes first in that order, and the remaining integral usually gets simpler.

faq.q: Is the test JEE Main or Advanced level?
faq.a: Both. It covers Main-level standard forms and a few Advanced-style substitutions, so it builds speed without a heavy time cost.
